case_title: Indrajit Sureshprasad Bind & Ors. v. State of Gujarat
neutral_facts: The accused, who were the husband and in-laws of the deceased, were alleged to have subjected the deceased to harassment and cruelty in connection with a demand for dowry, which led to her committing suicide by pouring kerosene on her body. The prosecution relied on a letter allegedly written by the deceased to her brother, which was the only evidence presented. However, there were doubts about the authenticity of the letter, as it was unclear whether it was written by the deceased or a man, and whether the deceased was at the location stated in the letter. Another letter from the deceased's brother to her, dated shortly before her death, indicated that he was satisfied she was living happily and not being misbehaved with. The prosecution failed to prove beyond reasonable doubt that the accused subjected the deceased to cruelty or harassment, and thus the conviction was overturned.
